10. Train, test & troubleshoot your SEO further Free Online SEO Courses & Training

Ready to learn SEO online with free, expert-backed courses and training? Whether you’re just starting your SEO journey or looking to advance your skills, this lesson brings together the most trusted free SEO courses from industry leaders like Moz, Semrush, and HubSpot.

From SEO fundamentals and technical optimization to content strategies and link building, these carefully curated courses cover every aspect of search engine optimization. Each free online SEO course has been selected for its practical value, clear instruction, and real-world application—helping you build skills that actually drive results.

You’ll find structured learning paths for beginners, specialized courses for technical SEO and local search, plus advanced training for those ready to tackle complex challenges. Many courses offer certificates upon completion, giving you credentials to showcase your expertise.

Start with the fundamentals if you’re new to SEO, or jump straight to specialized topics like link building or local SEO. With these free SEO training resources, you can learn at your own pace and build the skills needed to succeed in today’s competitive search landscape.

SEO Courses Learning Tips

Learn from experienced SEO professionals who share practical insights on finding the best SEO courses, study strategies, and how to apply your new knowledge effectively. These expert tips will help you maximize your learning experience and avoid common challenges as you build your SEO expertise.

Free courses always come with a catch. You’re either being sold a product, a service, or positioning in the market/industry – all of which are perfectly fine. But nothing is truly free.

Daniel K Cheung
X Linkedin Threads
Read the advice in the courses but don’t take them as gospel, experiment with the advice and try it out for yourself on your own website and test what works best and what doesn’t. Also, understand that what works for one niche might not work the same for another.
Nikki Halliwell
X Linkedin Threads
If a course is not educating you about things like – how search engines work (crawl, render and index), user intent, etc. Please don’t waste much of your time there. If they tell you to filter out your keywords based on high search volume only, please stay away from them.
Praveen Sharma
X Linkedin Threads
Practice makes perfect, even once you have taken the course the best thing you can do is put it into action and be prepared to fail, tweak things and try again. Even the best SEO’s don’t always get things right first time
Marion Leadbetter
X Linkedin Threads
Apply critical thinking – look the rational behind certain recommendations, question anything that is “guaranteed” and remember that there are rarely absolutes in SEO
Nati Elimelech
X Linkedin Threads
Practice it on your own site. Plus if you can, get a teacher. We learn when we can also ask questions and get the answers about what we are reading and implementing. Once we leave full time education it is more difficult to get the answers to the questions on real life examples.
Jo Turnbull
X Linkedin Threads
Perhaps you could recruit some seasoned folks in the community to help with restricted and limited-time Slack channels for learners to ask questions. No single bit of advice will be enough, but having someone they can @ for a short time could be really beneficial.
Keith Goode

1) Stay curious and keep asking questions. Find communities where you can discuss and debate learnings. 2) Nothing beats practical learning. You can develop your own site, or you can also help a friend’s site or find an internship/junior role to start testing things in real life.

Do all the courses but be very discerning. don’t take anything at face value. test and approve the things you’re learning and keep an open mind!

SEO Courses FAQs

Start with the SEO  fundamentals and continue with the area, whether technical, content, or link building, that is more attractive and relevant to your professional goals. 

 

It’s doable as long as you are disciplined and willing to invest your time also testing what you learn, ideally on your own site. If you can, have a mentor who can clarify doubts when they arise and be proactive to use other resources on this site when to complement and validate what you learn, especially when there are what could be seen as contradictions in the information you get. 

 

Remember that there are many ways to solve issues and challenges in SEO and their level of importance depends on the context, so it’s fundamental that you apply what you learn based on your own scenario, while understanding the concepts and prioritizing based on your own goals. What could seem like a contradiction might be just a difference in context. 

 

No, the only SEO tool that it’s a must-have to learn and do SEO is your own brain. Everything else will be an add-on to learn and accelerate the analysis and implementation of what you learn. Also, there are fantastic free tools listed here you can start using if you have minimal or no budget.

 

Google provides SEO guidelines and best practices, but doesn’t give free SEO courses. 

Yes! Many courses are designed specifically for beginners, starting with SEO fundamentals like how search engines work, basic keyword research, and on-page optimization. Look for courses labeled ‘SEO Fundamentals’ or ‘SEO for Beginners’ to start your learning journey.

Several courses provide certificates upon completion, including offerings from HubSpot, Semrush, and Google. These certificates can be valuable for showcasing your SEO knowledge to employers or clients. Check individual course descriptions for certification details.

Course duration varies widely—from quick 1-2 hour introductions to comprehensive programs spanning several weeks. Most beginner courses take 4-8 hours to complete, while advanced technical SEO courses may require 10-20 hours of study time.

Absolutely. These free SEO courses provide comprehensive education from industry experts. The key is combining course learning with hands-on practice. Start with fundamentals, then apply what you learn to real websites to reinforce your skills.

Begin with an SEO fundamentals course that covers search engine basics, keyword research, and on-page optimization. The Moz SEO Training Course and Google’s SEO Starter Guide are excellent starting points for building a strong foundation.
